title: Galois Closure of Q(2^(1/4)): Splitting Field of X^4-2 and its D4 Group

problemStatement.formal: K = \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt[4]{2},\, i) \text{ is the splitting field of } X^4 - 2 \text{ over } \mathbb{Q}, \quad [K : \mathbb{Q}] = 8, \quad \operatorname{Gal}(K/\mathbb{Q}) \cong D_4.
problemStatement.plain: The parent entry proves that $\sqrt[4]{2}$ has degree exactly 4 over $\mathbb{Q}$, but $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt[4]{2})$ is a *real* field and so contains only two of the four complex roots of $X^4 - 2$ (namely $\pm\sqrt[4]{2}$); the other two, $\pm i\sqrt[4]{2}$, are non-real. The smallest field in which $X^4 - 2$ factors completely — its splitting field, i.e. the Galois closure of $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt[4]{2})$ — is obtained by additionally adjoining $i$. We want to prove that this field is $K = \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt[4]{2}, i)$, that it has degree 8 over $\mathbb{Q}$, and that its group of $\mathbb{Q}$-automorphisms is the dihedral group of order 8, $D_4$ — the symmetry group of a square, generated by a rotation $r: \sqrt[4]{2}\mapsto i\sqrt[4]{2}$ (order 4) and a reflection $s$ (complex conjugation, order 2) with $srs = r^{-1}$.
